questions.prompt: After sources of power are identified, what question does Chapter 7 add?
choices: How to apply force through leverage
How to write more policies
How to protect every front equally
questions.explanation: Chapter 7 moves from found power to the problem of concentrated application.

questions.prompt: What best distinguishes leverage from broad effort?
choices: Leverage spreads force evenly
Leverage concentrates force where it changes outcomes most
Leverage avoids tradeoffs
questions.explanation: Leverage is concentrated force at the point of highest effect, not broad coverage.

questions.prompt: Why can a team with plenty of activity still have little leverage?
choices: Because activity can be spread across too many fronts
Because leverage always requires fewer people
Because leverage rejects all measurement
questions.explanation: High activity can coexist with low leverage when force is diffused instead of concentrated.

questions.prompt: In the school examples, what should leaders identify before concentrating force?
choices: The largest department
The pivot point that changes the rest
The most popular initiative
questions.explanation: A pivot point deserves concentration because it alters the payoff of later moves.

questions.prompt: Which pattern most strongly signals diffusion rather than leverage?
choices: One point gets enough force to unlock later gains
Every line gets a little attention and none changes much
A smaller move reshapes the rest of the system
questions.explanation: Diffusion spreads strength so widely that no point receives enough force to matter.

choices: It replaces power with balance
It applies force to the power source that was previously identified
It says power and leverage are unrelated
questions.explanation: Chapter 6 finds power; Chapter 7 shows how force should be concentrated on it.

questions.prompt: A household plan has one job that unlocks several others. What would leverage suggest?
choices: Spread effort equally across all tasks
Concentrate effort on the unlocking job first
Add more chores to keep momentum high
questions.explanation: Leverage favors concentrated force on the action that changes the rest of the system.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest sign that leverage is real?
choices: The plan looks balanced across teams
Force is concentrated at a point that changes the outcome disproportionately
The activity dashboard is full
questions.explanation: Real leverage shows up when force lands at the pivot point rather than being spread broadly.

questions.prompt: Why can broad coverage become weakness disguised as discipline?
choices: Because it removes all accountability
Because it thins force below the level needed to matter
Because it always costs more money
questions.explanation: Coverage can preserve motion while starving the crucial point of enough concentrated force.

questions.prompt: What chapter move naturally follows a clear understanding of leverage?
choices: Turning toward proximate objectives
Returning to generic effort language
Expanding every front at once
questions.explanation: Once leverage is clear, the next question is how to keep action focused step by step through proximate objectives.
